intro.text: The man Nomad calls Glowing Eyes, who confronts him when he first arrives on Canticle.
A Threnodite on Canticle who rules a flying city and leads its Charred.

items.text: Before he came to power, he served as an executioner. In that time he grew fascinated by the nature of power, deciding it was greater to have others follow his commands than simply to kill them.

He met a Thaylen worldhopper trying to make contact with the people of Canticle. Fearing a demon, he killed the man and took a set of encyclopedias from him, which told him of the wider cosmere and its peoples, and gave him the idea that he was destined to unite his planet.

He then began seizing power across Canticle, forming Union. At his height he held sway over every corridor and habitable region of the planet, controlling its people through violence and killing several off-worlders.

Several years before Nomad arrived, he gained access to the Scadrian research facility and struck a deal with the TimeTellers inside: he would supply sunhearts and whatever else their experiments needed, in exchange for advanced Scadrian knowledge and technology.

When Nomad arrived on Canticle, Glowing Eyes tried to question him but couldn't be understood, then laid hands on him, to no effect. When the crowd began to revere Nomad for escaping the sun, he hated it, and kicked Nomad repeatedly, enjoying that he didn't fight back.

He watched the arena contest closely, curious what Nomad could do, but his fighters singled Nomad out, making plain that he wanted the stranger killed in public. When Nomad defeated one of them, he activated Nomad's bracers and incapacitated him.

Stoking the crowd, he promised to make an example of Nomad. He killed two weak captives by draining their heat, then rammed a spear into a woman's chest, transforming her. Before he could do the same to another captive, Nomad threw his Shardblade into a pillar, stunning him.
He chose to transform Nomad instead, and Nomad spat on him. Before he could begin, rebels attacked the arena.

During the attack he took up a rifle and shot at a young rebel woman, nearly killing her several times, until Nomad shielded them with Auxiliary and drove him off with wild rifle fire. He didn't give chase himself, sending several ships after the rebels instead.

After Nomad and Rebeke downed a scout ship, Union's ruler came to inspect it in his personal ship and invited Nomad aboard, bringing flashcards to bridge the language gap. Surprised that Nomad could speak the local language, he offered to hire him as a mercenary and told how he had learned of the wider cosmere.
To show his power, he choked a Charred who couldn't fight back. When negotiations soured, he had Rebeke brought aboard and tried to shoot her, but Nomad intervened and they escaped.
He controls the Charred through his own cinderheart, which has not fully replaced his heart and so does not consume him. They hear his commands as a voice in their heads and feel his emotions.

Expecting trouble, he oversaw the collection of sunhearts himself, and caught Nomad stealing them. When Nomad refused to fight and fled, he sent Charred after him, and watched Nomad fight them off in a fear that passed to the Charred.

He brought dozens of ships and hundreds of Charred to defend the doorway to the Refuge, but the Beaconites' new ship-mounted guns scattered them. Thinking Zellion knew the Refuge's true location, he panicked and retreated to protect it, leading the Beaconites straight there, where his forces on the ground were scattered again.

When the Beaconites were refused entry to the Refuge, he took their sunhearts and left them for the sun, carrying Elegy and Rebeke back to Union. He believed he had put Elegy back under his control. Rebeke tried to trick him into sparing the Beaconites, but he decided to make her a Charred instead.

When Zellion flew after them, he had his engineers mount one of Beacon's guns and fired at him, but Elegy freed Charred from his control, spoiling his aim. Realizing she could think and remember, he threatened to kill Rebeke until she stopped, then locked down the city and ordered Rebeke taken to the Hall of Burning.

Zellion reached Union and challenged him to a duel, which he accepted. He weakened Zellion with snipers and Charred, fixed two bracers on him, one adding weight and one stealing warmth, and televised the fight, making a show of removing only the heat-stealing bracer.
Zellion pushed them both off the edge of Union to the ground. Meanwhile Rebeke persuaded the city to rebel, and it flew away, leaving him stranded with Zellion.
In a last attempt to survive, he tried to kill Zellion for his Shardblade, but Zellion drained his Investiture and Skipped away, leaving him to burn.

appearance.text: A tall man with glowing red eyes who looks about fifty but has not a single wrinkle. His cinderheart sits less deep in his chest than a Charred's, and some of its light shines through the black coat he covers it with.

personality.text: Obsessed with power, he believes it is his destiny to rule. He is interested in off-worlders mainly for their stories of conquest, and often cheats and lies to appear strong, insecure despite his boasting.
